mainTopic: Finishing the היקש about ברכת כהנים, then the משנה about מעמדות: why they exist, how the משמרות worked, who is indispensable for the קרבן, and how the 24 משמרות came about.
overview: First, the גמרא finishes an earlier discussion about the כהן who gives ברכת כהנים. He is compared both to a נזיר and to a כהן serving in the בית המקדש, and in each case we choose the lenient comparison, because these laws are מדרבנן and the verses are only an אסמכתא. Next, the גמרא turns to the משנה about מעמדות. It explains that the משנה means the verse 'Command the children of Israel... My offering' is the reason the מעמדות were set up. All of Israel owns the daily קרבנות, so each of the 24 משמרות had a matching מעמד of כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים. A ברייתא adds that half of each משמר lived in יריחו and supplied food and water to those serving in ירושלים. שמואל says כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים are indispensable for the קרבן, while רבי שמעון בן אלעזר lists musical instruments instead of ישראלים; the dispute is whether the לויים' song is mainly vocal or instrumental. The גמרא then discusses how the משמרות grew to 24: רב says משה made 8, but another ברייתא says 16, and the answer is that תנאים disagree. Finally, a ברייתא begins describing how only four משמרות returned from בבל, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Should a blemished כהן be barred from blessing?
steps.stepSummary: If the blessing כהן is compared to the serving כהן, then a בעל מום should not be allowed to bless.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then just as a ministering כהן may not be a בעל מום, so too a כהן who blesses may not be a בעל מום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the earlier comparison further. If the blessing כהן is like the serving כהן, then a physically blemished כהן should be forbidden to bless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא compared the blessing כהן to a serving כהן (משרת) in order to be lenient about grape pits. Now it asks whether that same comparison should also bring a stringency: a serving כהן with a מום is disqualified, so maybe a blessing כהן with a מום is disqualified too.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן who serves (does the עבודה) in the בית המקדש
Someone with a physical blemish
A כהן who gives ברכת כהנים
So too / also

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה מְשָׁרֵת — בַּעַל מוּם לָא,
phrases.english: If so: just as a ministering priest — a blemished one may not [serve],
phrases.notes: Builds on the earlier comparison of the blessing priest to the serving priest.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּהֵן מְבָרֵךְ — בַּעַל מוּם לָא!
phrases.english: so too a priest who blesses — a blemished one may not [bless]!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the היקש between the blessing כהן and the serving כהן, which comes on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: The היקש of the blessing כהן to the serving כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison works for one detail, it should carry over the serving כהן's disqualification of a בעל מום as well.

steps.title: He is also compared to a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The blessing כהן is also compared to a נזיר, and a נזיר is not disqualified by a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is also compared to a נזיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the blessing כהן is not compared only to the serving כהן. He is also compared to a נזיר, and a מום does not disqualify a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessing כהן is linked to two different models. On the question of a מום, the גמרא follows the נזיר model, which has no rule against a מום, so the blemished כהן may still bless.

keyTerms.meaning: He was compared by a היקש (a comparison drawn from verses placed together)
A person who took a vow to avoid wine and grape products

phrases.english: But he is [also] juxtaposed to a nazirite.
phrases.notes: A נזיר has no disqualification for a blemish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a second comparison that leads to the opposite result
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Comparing him to the serving כהן means a בעל מום cannot bless.
steps.terutzMaskana: Comparing him to the נזיר means a מום does not disqualify him.

steps.title: Why compare leniently and not strictly?
steps.stepSummary: Why choose the lenient side of each comparison? We could just as easily choose the strict side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what made you decide to compare him leniently? Compare him strictly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the method itself. Why do we always pick whichever comparison is more lenient, instead of whichever is stricter?
steps.deeperAnalysis: For grape pits, we compared him to the serving כהן, which is lenient. For a מום, we compared him to the נזיר, which is also lenient. One could just as easily do the reverse: compare him to the נזיר and forbid grape pits, and compare him to the serving כהן and disqualify a בעל מום.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why did you choose this way over the other?)
To be lenient
To be strict

phrases.english: And what did you see that you juxtaposed [him] for a leniency?
Juxtapose [him] for a stringency!
phrases.notes: That would mean forbidding grape pits (like a נזיר) and disqualifying a blemished כהן (like a משרת).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the method used to answer step 1 (and the earlier grape pits case).
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice to always take the lenient side of each comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two comparisons point in opposite directions, and nothing obvious tells us to prefer the lenient one.

steps.title: Rabbinic laws, so we are lenient
steps.stepSummary: These verses only serve as a support (אסמכתא) for rabbinic laws, so we apply them leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are only an אסמכתא for laws that are מדרבנן, so we go lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that these laws come from the רבנן, not the תורה. The verses are only a hint attached to them, so whenever there is doubt we choose the lenient side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אסמכתא is not a true source; it is a verse the רבנן connect to a law they made. Because the law is מדרבנן, we do not stretch these comparisons to create extra stringencies.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse used as a support or hint for a rabbinic law, not as its real source
A law from the רבנן, not from the תורה

steps.whatToRemember: The blessing כהן is compared to both a נזיר and a serving כהן. In every case we take the lenient comparison, because these rules are rabbinic and the verses are only an אסמכתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule: when a verse is only an אסמכתא for a rabbinic law, we do not build stringencies from it.

phrases.english: They are [merely] supports for rabbinic law, and [so we apply them] for a leniency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 and closes the topic.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the legal level of the law (rabbinic), which decides the direction of the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Either comparison could be applied, strict or lenient.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the laws are מדרבנן and the verses only an אסמכתא, we always apply them leniently.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: 'These are the מעמדות, since it says: Command the children of Israel.'
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the מעמדות. Since it says: 'Command the children of Israel...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the opening line of the משנה about מעמדות. This line sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording seems to jump. It says 'these are the מעמדות' and right away says 'since it is stated,' quoting a verse, without saying what the verse is meant to prove.

keyTerms.meaning: Groups (mainly ישראלים) who stood as representatives of all Israel while the קרבנות were brought
Since it is stated

phrases.english: These are the non-priestly watches.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״צַו אֶת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כּוּ׳״.
phrases.english: Since it is stated: "Command the children of Israel, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the משנה about מעמדות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעמדות are grounded in the verse 'Command the children of Israel.'

steps.title: What is the משנה saying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the משנה's words fit together.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means. How does the verse connect to the words 'these are the מעמדות'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'since it is stated' needs something to explain, but the משנה only said 'these are the מעמדות.' The גמרא wants to know what point the verse is proving.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it saying?

phrases.english: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the verse relates to the words 'these are the מעמדות.'

steps.title: The verse gives the reason for the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means: these are the מעמדות, and the reason they were set up is the verse 'my offering... you shall observe.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: These are the מעמדות. And why did they set up מעמדות? Because it says: 'Command the children of Israel and say to them: My offering, My food, for My fires.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that there is an unstated question in the משנה: why were the מעמדות made? The verse is the answer to that question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse commands all of Israel to bring the daily קרבנות. These are bought with public funds, so they belong to everyone, and all of Israel needs some form of presence when they are brought. That is the reason for the מעמדות.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (the גמרא fills in a missing step)
They instituted (set up)
'My offering, My food, for My fires' (from the verse)

phrases.english: This is what it is saying: These are the non-priestly watches.
And what is the reason they instituted the non-priestly watches?
Since it is stated: "Command the children of Israel

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַרְתָּ אֲלֵיהֶם אֶת קׇרְבָּנִי לַחְמִי לְאִשַּׁי״.
phrases.english: and say to them: My offering, My food, for My fires."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה leaves out the words 'and why were they instituted'; the verse answers that question.

steps.title: How can an offering be brought without its owner?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks: how can a person's קרבן be offered when he is not standing there?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how can a person's offering be brought while he is not standing next to it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a question. All of Israel owns the daily קרבנות, but they cannot all be in the בית המקדש. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner is supposed to be present for his קרבן. Since the public offerings belong to everyone, the משנה asks how this can work in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: And how?
Standing over it (being present at it)

phrases.english: But how can a person's offering be sacrificed
while he is not standing next to it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's reasoning from the verse in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How all of Israel can be present for the public קרבנות.

steps.title: Twenty-four משמרות and their מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים הראשונים set up 24 משמרות. Each had a matching מעמד in ירושלים of כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים. When a משמר's turn came, its כהנים and לויים went up to ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The early prophets set up 24 משמרות. For each משמר there was a מעמד in ירושלים of כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים. When it was time for a משמר to go up, the כהנים and לויים went up to ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the question. A rotating system of groups let representatives of all Israel stand by the קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the 24 כהונה shifts had a matching group of ישראלים who acted as representatives of the whole nation. This solves the problem of the owners being absent. The משנה starts describing who actually went up to ירושלים, beginning with the כהנים and לויים.

keyTerms.meaning: The early prophets (שמואל and דוד)
The rotating shifts of כהנים who served in the בית המקדש
The time arrived
Go up

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up משמר and מעמד. A משמר is a shift of כהנים who actually serve. A מעמד is the matching group (mostly ישראלים) who stand as representatives of the nation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the purpose of the מעמדות: they let the public offerings truly be brought on behalf of all Israel.

phrases.english: The early prophets instituted
twenty-four priestly watches.
For each and every priestly watch
there was a [corresponding] watch in Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים וְשֶׁל לְוִיִּם וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: of priests, of Levites, and of Israelites.
When the time arrived for a watch to ascend,
the priests and Levites would ascend to Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through 24 משמרות, each with a representative מעמד of כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים.

steps.title: A ברייתא: 24 משמרות in ארץ ישראל and 12 in יריחו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא saying there were 24 משמרות in ארץ ישראל and 12 in יריחו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There were twenty-four משמרות in ארץ ישראל, and twelve in יריחו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with more detail about the משמרות. This sets up the next move, because the numbers in it will cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the ברייתא says there were 24 משמרות in ארץ ישראל and another 12 in יריחו. That adds new information about יריחו, which our משנה did not mention.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
Jericho, a city near ירושלים
The rotating groups of כהנים who served in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Twenty-four priestly watches in Eretz Yisrael,
and twelve in Jericho.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the description of the משמרות in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were 24 משמרות in ארץ ישראל and 12 in יריחו

steps.title: Twelve in יריחו? That is too many
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that adding 12 in יריחו would give too many משמרות, 36 in total.
steps.simpleTranslation: Twelve in Jericho?! That makes far too many of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the simple reading of the ברייתא. If there were 24 plus 12, the total would be 36, but everyone knows there were only 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number 24 is fixed, as step 9 already said. So reading the ברייתא as "24 and an extra 12" cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: They are too many

phrases.english: Twelve in Jericho?!
There are far too many of them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement of 12 משמרות in יריחו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There were only 24 משמרות. Adding 12 more would give 36, which is impossible.

steps.title: Twelve of the 24 lived in יריחו and supplied food and water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the ברייתא: 12 of the 24 lived in יריחו. Half of each משמר came from יריחו to supply food and water to those in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: twelve of them were in יריחו. When the time came for a משמר to go up, half of the משמר went up from all over ארץ ישראל to ירושלים, and half went up from יריחו, in order to supply water and food to their brothers in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading of the ברייתא. The 12 in יריחו are not extra; they are part of the 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "מהן" (of them) changes everything: 12 out of the 24, not 12 more. The ברייתא then explains why יריחו is mentioned. The half that lived there brought supplies, so the כהנים serving in ירושלים had water and food.

keyTerms.meaning: Of them, meaning part of the 24
Half of the priestly watch
So that they would supply water and food

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count 36 משמרות. The total stays 24; יריחו was simply home to part of them.

phrases.english: Rather: twelve of them were in Jericho.
When the time came for the watch to go up,
half of the watch would go up
from Eretz Yisrael to Jerusalem,
and half of the watch would go up from Jericho,
in order to supply water and food
to their brothers in Jerusalem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 12 extra משמרות in יריחו, for a total of 36
steps.terutzMaskana: 12 of the 24 were based in יריחו and provided supplies for those in ירושלים

steps.title: שמואל: כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים are indispensable for the קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: the קרבן cannot be brought without כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים are indispensable for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about the מעמדות. All three groups must be present for the קרבן תמיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ties back to our משנה: the ישראלים of the מעמד must stand by the קרבן, so they are not optional. Without all three groups, the קרבן is held back.

keyTerms.meaning: Are indispensable; without them the thing cannot be done
Offering, here the קרבן תמיד

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Priests, Levites, and Israelites
are indispensable for the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic building on the three-part מעמד described in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לויים, and ישראלים are all indispensable for the קרבן

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: כהנים, לויים, and musical instruments are indispensable
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: כהנים, לויים, and musical instruments are indispensable for the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a ברייתא, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר taught: כהנים, לויים, and musical instruments are indispensable for the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different opinion. The third item on the list is musical instruments instead of ישראלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both lists include כהנים and לויים. The difference is the third item: שמואל lists ישראלים, while רבי שמעון בן אלעזר lists כלי שיר. This sets up the question of what they disagree about.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Musical instruments played by the לויים

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר:
phrases.english: In a baraita Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar taught:
Priests, Levites, and musical instruments
are indispensable for the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing list to שמואל's statement in step 13
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים, לויים, and כלי שיר are indispensable for the קרבן

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle שמואל and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagree about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the two different lists. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants to find the underlying idea that explains why one requires instruments and the other does not.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root of the dispute between steps 13 and 14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The principle behind the dispute between שמואל and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר

steps.title: Is the main part of the שירה the voice or the instrument?
steps.stepSummary: One holds that the main part of the שירה is vocal; the other holds it is played on instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: One Sage holds that the main part of the song is with the mouth, and the other Sage holds that the main part of the song is with an instrument.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the dispute is about the nature of the לויים' song.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל holds that the main part of the שירה is singing with the mouth, so instruments are not indispensable. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that the main part is the instrument, so the כלי שיר are indispensable for the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: The essential part of the לויים' song
With the mouth (vocal)
With an instrument

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute over who is indispensable for the קרבן comes down to one question: is the שירה mainly vocal (שמואל) or mainly instrumental (רבי שמעון בן אלעזר)?

phrases.english: One Sage holds: the main part of the song is with the mouth,
and one Sage holds: the main part of the song is with an instrument.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שמואל: the שירה is mainly vocal; רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: the שירה is mainly instrumental

steps.title: רב: the משמרות grew from 8 to 16 to 24
steps.stepSummary: רב says משה set up 8 משמרות, שמואל expanded them to 16, and דוד expanded them to 24, with a verse from דברי הימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: משה set up eight משמרות for Israel, four from אלעזר and four from איתמר. שמואל came and made them sixteen. דוד came and made them twenty-four, as it says: "In the fortieth year of דוד's reign they were sought out, and mighty men of valor were found among them at Jazer of Gilead."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a history of the משמרות. They were not always 24; they grew in three stages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each stage came from a different leader: משה (8), שמואל (16), then דוד (24). The verse about the fortieth year of דוד's reign shows that דוד was the one who completed the system.

keyTerms.meaning: Instituted, set up
The two surviving sons of אהרן, ancestors of all כהנים
He set them at (a number)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
Moses instituted for Israel
eight priestly watches,
four from Elazar and four from Itamar.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא שְׁמוּאֵל וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה,
phrases.english: Samuel came and set them at sixteen,

phrases.aramaic: בָּא דָּוִד וְהֶעֱמִידָן עַל עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה,
phrases.english: David came and set them at twenty-four,
as it is stated: "In the fortieth year of the reign of David
they were sought out, and there were found among them
mighty men of valor at Jazer of Gilead" (I Chronicles 26:31).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the history of how the 24 משמרות came about
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה set up 8, שמואל set up 16, and דוד set up 24

steps.title: A ברייתא says דוד and שמואל together made 24
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says דוד and שמואל together brought the משמרות to 24, which seems to contradict רב's three stages.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: משה set up eight משמרות for Israel, four from אלעזר and four from איתמר, and דוד and שמואל came and made them twenty-four, as it says: "Whom דוד and שמואל the seer established in their trust."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב with a ברייתא that skips the stage of 16. It says דוד and שמואל jointly brought the number to 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives שמואל credit for 16 and דוד for 24. The ברייתא names both together for 24, which suggests there was no separate stage of 16 under שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (usually from a ברייתא)
שמואל the seer (the נביא)
Founded, established

phrases.english: They raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: מֹשֶׁה תִּיקֵּן לָהֶם לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שְׁמוֹנָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת,
phrases.english: Moses instituted for Israel eight priestly watches,
four from Elazar and four from Itamar,
and David and Samuel came
and set them at twenty-four,
as it is stated: "Whom David established
and Samuel the seer, in their trust" (I Chronicles 9:22)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's statement in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's claim that שמואל made 16 and דוד made 24
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא and verse credit דוד and שמואל jointly with reaching 24, with no separate stage of 16

steps.title: Building on what דוד and שמואל founded, they reached 24
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the ברייתא: the 24 came out of the system founded by שמואל and דוד, step by step.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: from the foundation laid by דוד and שמואל of Ramah, they set them at twenty-four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא does not contradict רב. It means the final 24 grew out of what both of them established.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as describing the result, not one single joint act. שמואל built the first stage (16) and דוד completed it (24), so both are credited with the founding. This fits רב's three stages.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means
From the foundation of
From Ramah, שמואל's hometown

steps.whatToRemember: The משמרות grew in stages: משה set up 8, שמואל set up 16, and דוד set up 24. Both שמואל and דוד are credited because the 24 grew out of their combined foundation.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
from the foundation of David and Samuel of Ramah
they set them at twenty-four.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: דוד and שמואל together jumped from 8 to 24
steps.terutzMaskana: The 24 resulted, in stages, from the foundation laid by שמואל and דוד, which matches רב

steps.title: A second ברייתא: משה set up sixteen watches
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says משה set up 16 משמרות, 8 from אלעזר and 8 from איתמר. When בני אלעזר grew, they were split to make 24 in total. Two verses are brought as support.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: משה set up sixteen watches for Israel, eight from אלעזר and eight from איתמר. When the descendants of אלעזר grew more than the descendants of איתמר, they divided them and made them twenty-four. As it says: 'More leaders were found among בני אלעזר than among בני איתמר, so they divided them: sixteen family heads for בני אלעזר and eight for בני איתמר.' And it also says: 'One family house taken for אלעזר, and taken, taken for איתמר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a different count. It says משה started with 16 משמרות, not 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב (quoted by רב חמא בר גוריא in step 17), משה set up only 8 משמרות. This ברייתא says משה set up 16, and only בני אלעזר grew from 8 to 16, which makes 24. That already sets the ground for a challenge to רב חמא בר גוריא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in another ברייתא
Priestly watches, the groups of כהנים who took turns serving in the מקדש
The two surviving sons of אהרן, from whom all כהנים descend
A family house, a sub-group within a watch
Taken or assigned, meaning a portion set aside

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the numbers. Here משה starts with 16 (8+8). Only אלעזר's side doubles to 16, so 16+8 = 24.

phrases.english: It was taught in another baraita:
Moses instituted for Israel
sixteen priestly watches,
eight from Elazar and eight from Itamar.

phrases.aramaic: וּכְשֶׁרַבּוּ בְּנֵי אֶלְעָזָר עַל בְּנֵי אִיתָמָר,
phrases.english: And when the sons of Elazar became more numerous than the sons of Itamar,
they divided them and set them at twenty-four,
as it says: 'And the sons of Elazar were found more numerous
in chief men than the sons of Itamar
and they divided them: for the sons of Elazar
sixteen heads of fathers' houses
and for the sons of Itamar, by their fathers' houses, eight'
And it says: 'One father's house taken for Elazar
and taken, taken for Itamar.'
phrases.notes: I Chronicles 24:6. This means the portions for איתמר stayed as they were.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ברייתא with a different original count than רב's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה set up 16 משמרות (8+8). בני אלעזר later grew to 16, for a total of 24.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא need a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא added 'and it says' with a second verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא brought a second verse when the first one seems to be enough. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first verse already gives 16 for אלעזר and 8 for איתמר. So the גמרא wants to know what extra point the second verse proves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says', which introduces an additional verse

phrases.english: What is 'and it says' for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the purpose of the second verse in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second verse proves that the first verse does not.

steps.title: The second verse proves בני איתמר did not grow
steps.stepSummary: Without the second verse, one might think בני איתמר also grew from 4 to 8. The second verse shows that איתמר's portion stayed the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: just as בני אלעזר grew, so too בני איתמר grew, and their eight were originally four. Come and hear: 'One father's house taken for אלעזר, and taken, taken for איתמר.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second verse blocks a mistaken reading. Someone might think איתמר's 8 used to be only 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From the first verse alone, one could argue, as רב חמא בר גוריא does, that both families grew: בני איתמר went from 4 to 8, just as בני אלעזר grew. The second verse ('אחז אחז לאיתמר') shows that איתמר's share stayed the same. So their 8 were 8 from the start, and משה's original total was 16.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say, which introduces a possible mistaken thought
They increased, they became many
Originally, at first
Come and hear, which introduces a proof

phrases.english: And if you would say:
just as the sons of Elazar increased,
so too here the sons of Itamar increased —
the eight were originally four,

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״בֵּית אָב אֶחָד אָחֻז לְאֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: come and hear: 'One father's house taken for Elazar
and taken, taken for Itamar.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the second verse.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second verse proves that איתמר's 8 were always 8, so the original total was 16.

steps.title: A refutation of רב חמא בר גוריא
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא proves משה started with 16, it refutes רב חמא בר גוריא, who said משה started with 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב חמא בר גוריא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that this ברייתא seems to completely knock down רב חמא בר גוריא's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חמא בר גוריא (quoting רב in step 17) said משה made 8, which requires איתמר to have started with only 4. The ברייתא's second verse says איתמר never grew. So his three-stage count seems disproven.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation, a strong challenge that seems to disprove a view
The אמורא who reported רב's statement about 8, 16, and 24

steps.confusionAlert: Step 17 was listed as 'רב says', but the statement was reported by רב חמא בר גוריא in רב's name. That is why the challenge is directed at him.

phrases.english: A refutation of Rav Ḥama bar Gurya!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the explanation in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חמא בר גוריא's claim that משה set up 8 משמרות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא proves איתמר always had 8, so משה must have started with 16, not 8.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא answers that תנאים disagree about the original number, and he follows the תנא who said 8.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא can tell you: it is a dispute between תנאים, and I said my view like the תנא who said eight.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חמא בר גוריא. The second ברייתא is just one opinion, and he holds like the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier ברייתא (step 18) supports a count that began with 8. Since two ברייתות disagree, a ברייתא against him does not refute him. He simply sides with the first תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
He could say to you, which introduces a defense on someone's behalf

steps.whatToRemember: How many משמרות משה set up is a dispute between תנאים: one says 8, another says 16. Either way, the final number was 24.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya could say to you:
it is a dispute of tanna'im,
and I, what I said
is like that tanna who said eight.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא of step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second ברייתא is decisive and disproves רב חמא בר גוריא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות disagree, and רב חמא בר גוריא follows the תנא who said 8.

steps.title: Only four watches returned from the exile
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says only four משמרות came back from בבל: ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, and אמר. The prophets among them then stood up to act.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Four watches came up from the exile, and these are they: ידעיה, חרים, פשחור, and אמר. The prophets among them stood up...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about what happened to the משמרות after the exile. This passage stops in the middle, setting up what the prophets did next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Of the 24 משמרות, only 4 returned to ארץ ישראל. This creates a problem: how could the 24-week rotation continue? The next part explains how the prophets solved it.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught, which introduces a ברייתא
Went up from the exile (בבל)
The four watches that returned
Prophets

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Four priestly watches went up from the exile,
and these are they:
Jedaiah, Harim, Pashhur, and Immer.
The prophets among them arose,
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת עָלוּ מִן הַגּוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the original setup of the משמרות to their state after the exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only four משמרות returned from בבל, and the prophets then acted to restore the system.
